name: AI Now Institute
what: AI Now Institute is an independent research institute providing expert analysis on artificial intelligence in the public interest.
tags: AI; research; policy; public interest

name: American Foundation for the Blind
what: The American Foundation for the Blind works to expand possibilities for the millions of Americans living with vision loss, and has done so since 1921.
tags: accessibility; blindness; vision loss; nonprofit

name: Ballotpedia
what: Ballotpedia is a digital encyclopedia of American politics, covering elections, candidates, and ballot measures.
tags: elections; politics; reference; voting

name: Beeck Center for Social Impact and Innovation
what: The Beeck Center at Georgetown University works on building a people-centred, digitally enabled government for all.
tags: govtech; research; public interest technology; university

name: Benetech
what: Benetech is a nonprofit that creates software for social good in education, employment, and social inclusion, and offers free training for educators supporting students with diverse learning needs.
tags: accessibility; education; software for good; nonprofit

name: CarbonPlan
what: CarbonPlan works on the transparency and scientific integrity of climate solutions, publishing open data and tools alongside its analysis.
tags: climate; open data; research; tools

name: Center for Civic Design
what: The Center for Civic Design works on election design, so that voters can express their intent clearly. It publishes its research and field guides for election officials.
tags: elections; design; accessibility; research

name: Center for Tech and Civic Life
what: The Center for Tech and Civic Life works with election officials to modernise the American voting experience, through grants, research, and shared election infrastructure.
tags: elections; civic tech; grants; research

name: Code for America
what: Code for America works with governments and communities across the country to break down barriers and find real solutions, and believes government at every level can work well for everyone.
tags: civic tech; government; digital services; nonprofit

name: CodeAI
what: CodeAI is an education nonprofit working so that every student in every school can learn about artificial intelligence and computer science as part of their core K-12 education. It was previously known as Code.org.
tags: computer science; education; K-12; AI

name: Coding it Forward
what: Coding it Forward is a nonprofit for early-career technologists. It runs the Coding it Forward Fellowship, a civic tech internship for students and recent graduates.
tags: public interest technology; fellowship; students; civic tech

name: Community Solutions
what: Community Solutions helps communities act with speed, coordination, and accountability to reduce homelessness, and publishes data on the progress those communities make.
tags: homelessness; housing; data; nonprofit

name: Crisis Text Line
what: Crisis Text Line provides free, 24-hour, confidential text support for people in crisis, in English and Spanish.
tags: mental health; crisis support; text messaging; nonprofit

name: Data & Society Research Institute
what: Data & Society is a research institute studying the social implications of data and automation. It argues that technology policy should be grounded in research about technology's real-world effects.
tags: research; technology policy; data; society

name: DataKind
what: DataKind works with social sector organisations to design data science and AI projects in areas including health, humanitarian action, climate, and education.
tags: data science; nonprofit; volunteers; AI

name: Democracy Works
what: Democracy Works builds tools and delivers election information that help millions of Americans vote, with the aim of removing the gaps that keep turnout low.
tags: voting; elections; civic tech; information

name: Electronic Frontier Foundation
what: The Electronic Frontier Foundation defends civil liberties in the digital world. It litigates, campaigns, and publishes tools and guides on privacy, free speech, creativity, and surveillance.
tags: digital rights; privacy; free speech; surveillance

name: EveryoneOn
what: EveryoneOn connects under-resourced communities to affordable internet and computers, trains people and organisations in digital skills, and works for fair access policies.
tags: digital inclusion; affordable internet; devices; digital skills

name: Feeding America
what: Feeding America is a nonprofit network of 200 food banks working to end hunger in the United States.
tags: food security; food banks; hunger; nonprofit

name: Freedom of the Press Foundation
what: Freedom of the Press Foundation builds and supports secure tools for journalists, and campaigns against threats to press freedom.
tags: press freedom; journalism; security tools; encryption

name: GovTrack
what: GovTrack tracks legislation and votes in the United States Congress and actions by the White House, and publishes the record where anyone can follow it.
tags: congress; legislation; transparency; open data

name: Kapor Center
what: The Kapor Center is a family of organisations working to remove barriers for people of colour in the technology sector, through research, programmes, advocacy, and investment.
tags: racial equity; tech sector; research; investment

name: Knowbility
what: Knowbility is a nonprofit based in Austin, Texas working to create an inclusive digital world for people with disabilities, through training, consulting, and advocacy. It was founded in 1999.
tags: accessibility; disability; training; consulting

name: Open States
what: Open States publishes data on state legislatures across the United States. It covers who the legislators are, what they sponsor, and how they vote.
tags: state legislatures; open data; legislation; api

name: ProPublica
what: ProPublica is an independent, non-profit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest.
tags: investigative journalism; nonprofit news; public interest

name: Public Knowledge
what: Public Knowledge promotes freedom of expression, an open internet, and access to affordable communications tools and creative works, through policy work on behalf of the public interest.
tags: internet policy; open internet; free expression; advocacy

name: Rewiring America
what: Rewiring America works on electrifying American households, with the aim of clean energy that every household can afford.
tags: electrification; clean energy; households; climate

name: U.S. Federation of Worker Cooperatives
what: The U.S. Federation of Worker Cooperatives is the national membership organisation for worker cooperatives and democratic workplaces. It represents an estimated 1,300 US worker co-ops and their 15,000 workers.
tags: worker cooperatives; economic democracy; membership; advocacy

name: USAFacts
what: USAFacts publishes a nonpartisan view of the state of the country, built from government data and free for anyone to use.
tags: open data; government data; statistics; nonpartisan

name: Vote.org
what: Vote.org is a nonpartisan service for registering to vote, checking a registration, and requesting an absentee ballot.
tags: voting; registration; elections; nonpartisan
